correctness.rationale: The corrected set T has eight possible members, each a subset of the three generator names. A complement to the sum removes B_empty. A projection onto the triple intersection splits it from all three. Each remaining pair intersection is disjoint from the third subspace, so a projection onto it killing the third splits all three compatibly. Once pair intersections vanish, a complement inside one subspace to its intersection with the sum of the others splits by a projection killing those others. Previously acquired sum inclusions are preserved by the complementary projection. The three residual subspaces are pairwise disjoint and each pair spans; identifying the third as a graph of an isomorphism gives copies of the three-line plane over any field, including F_2. On a line block indexed by R, E_S fails exactly at R=S; on the plane, E_S always holds and E_triangle alone fails. Bounds and all recursively generated terms evaluate componentwise, with identical marked two-element chains or three-atom diamonds across fields, so term equality is completely determined by which blocks appear, not by multiplicity. Identical term kernels give precisely the marked bounded isomorphisms, including the one-element algebra in dimension zero. Each selected line contributes dimension one and each plane two, yielding the minimum |T|+2ε, all extra dimensions with any line present, and only positive even dimensions when the plane alone is present. Summing nonempty line supports at the two thresholds plus the even plane-only case gives N(n); independent realization of all 512 kernels forces at least nine yes/no tests.
residual_risks: The replay is of the finite term model, not a general-field subspace enumeration. The reduction and cross-field comparison supply the universal argument. The statement does not classify unmarked lattices or full first-order theories.
